written_before_any_run: Committed before the code or any run. Question: if v2 drops the separate calibration set and trains on those rows too, does the model get better?
question: Does training on development plus calibration rows (about 80% of the data) beat training on development rows only (about 60%)?
inputs: The five inputs plus the Eircode routing key, as in the current v2 candidate, with the v1 tuned settings.

design.scored_rows: The same 4,882 development rows in the same five group folds, in both arms. Only these rows are ever scored.
design.arm_a_60: For each fold, train on the other four development folds (the current setup).
design.arm_b_80: For each fold, train on the other four development folds PLUS every calibration row that has a floor area.
design.what_is_read: Calibration rows are read as training rows only. Their prices are never scored here. The final test is not read.
design.why_fair: Same scored rows, same folds, same model settings. The only difference is the extra training rows, so any change is down to more data.

adopt_rule: Drop the separate calibration set for v2 only if ALL hold: (1) arm B has at least 0.3 points lower CV MAPE than arm A in BOTH models; (2) arm B is lower in at least 4 of the 5 folds in both models; (3) arm B's median over or under estimate stays within plus or minus 2%, so it does not win by estimating low.
if_adopted: v2 trains on the 80%, sets its accuracy threshold and its price range from out-of-fold predictions, and is judged once on the untouched final test. The v2 final test checks that this threshold holds.
also_report: MdAPE, within 10%, MAE, R2 and the median signed error, plus the number of training rows in each arm.
nothing_else_changes: The frozen v1 model, its split and its final test are untouched.
